# University College London (UCL) – Concise Summary
University College London (UCL), established in 1826 as the first secular university in England, was created as an inclusive alternative to the religious universities of Oxford and Cambridge. Its foundation emphasized science, political economy, and the early admission of women to degree programs. UCL is now a constituent college of the University of London, and was officially granted full university status in 2023, allowing it to confer its own degrees. The university has a rich tradition of innovation and inclusion, leading in areas like the creation of engineering and chemical engineering departments, pioneering medical education, and establishing open access publishing through UCL Press.
Based primarily in the Bloomsbury area of Central London, UCL has recently expanded to UCL East near the Olympic Park. With over 46,000 students (majority international), UCL is organized into eleven faculties covering arts, sciences, engineering, medicine, law, education, and more. It is recognized globally for its research excellence, high external income, robust intellectual property portfolio, and sustainability leadership. UCL consistently ranks among the top universities worldwide, supports a wide range of research centers and museums, and counts 33 Nobel Prize laureates among its alumni and staff. Student life is vibrant, with 250+ clubs, a tradition of secularism, competitive sports and a history of activism.
